subject: SIG Q02.a - clarification on 'ownership of encryption key rotation' and evidence package
messages:
From: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@finbank.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Bob Lee <bob.lee@finbank.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: SIG Q02.a - clarification needed on key rotation ownership

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking our SIG. Q02.a asks: 'Describe who is responsible for encryption key rotation and the mechanism by which rotation is performed and audited.' The phrasing is a bit ambiguous for our procurement review — specifically:

- Do you interpret 'who is responsible' as Redwood (service level) vs customer (customer-managed keys)?
- For multi-tenant hosted offering, do you provide per-tenant keys or a platform-managed key with access controls?

Can you provide a clear written interpretation we can include in our SIG answers, plus the supporting evidence you would attach (e.g., architecture diagram, KMS config snapshot, policy excerpt)? If you can, please also propose a brief time window for a call to walk the SecOps team through the flow.

Appreciate it—we're trying to close this item for our internal legal/compliance review by end of week.

Best,
Alice Morgan
Senior Security Analyst, FinBank

[Attachment: finbank-sig-q-list.pdf]

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@finbank.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG Q02.a - clarification needed on key rotation ownership

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear note. Short answer up front: Redwood interprets Q02.a as asking for both (a) our default production behavior for hosted customers and (b) the options we offer when customers bring their own key material (BYOK). Below is a concise written interpretation you can paste into your SIG response, followed by the evidence we plan to attach. If that looks good, we can schedule a 30-minute call to walk the flow.

Proposed written interpretation (please confirm):
"For Redwood's hosted API, key rotation is performed by Redwood's platform KMS for platform-managed cryptographic keys; rotation schedules, key lifecycle operations, and audit trails are controlled by Redwood. For customers who opt for customer-managed keys (BYOK), the customer retains control over rotation and Redwood integrates with customer KMS via external key references (e.g., AWS KMS External Key), in which case Redwood does not perform rotation — We document the integration points and required configuration for customer key rotation. Evidence: architecture diagram showing KMS boundary, KMS policy excerpt, rotation audit log sample, and a short runbook describing responsibilities."

Planned evidence bundle: 
- redwood-kms-ownership-diagram.pdf (high-level boundary + per-tenant vs platform-managed flow)
- sig-evidence-checklist.xlsx (mapping of SIG Q02.a to artifacts)
- rotation-audit-sample.log (redacted) — will provide as text stub
- runbook-excerpt.txt (responsibility matrix for platform vs BYOK)

Proposed times for a call: Wed 2026-08-18 15:00-16:00 PDT or Thu 2026-08-19 09:00-12:00 PDT. If those don't work, suggest alternatives and we'll try to accommodate.

Cc'ing Neha (Security) and Ben (Solutions) to validate the artifacts.

—Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

[Attachments to follow: redwood-kms-ownership-diagram.pdf, sig-evidence-checklist.xlsx]

From: Bob Lee <bob.lee@finbank.com>

Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 13:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG Q02.a - clarification needed on key rotation ownership

Thanks, Irene — that wording is helpful. A couple of quick clarifications before the call:

1) For BYOK scenarios, can Redwood confirm whether you persist any key material, or only references/ARNS to the customer KMS?
2) For platform-managed keys, can you confirm rotation frequency default and whether customers can request a custom rotation cadence?

We prefer Thu 2026-08-19 10:00-10:30 PDT if that slot is available. If you can send the diagram ahead of the call, that'd be ideal so our SecOps folks can review.

—Bob
Bob Lee
Senior Compliance Manager, FinBank

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Bob Lee <bob.lee@finbank.com>, Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@finbank.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG Q02.a - clarification needed on key rotation ownership

Bob/Alice — quick internal alignment + answers to your two bullets before the call: 

- BYOK: Redwood does NOT persist customer private key material. We store only a reference/ARN and metadata needed to access the key (e.g., KMS key ARN, access role). We will include a config snapshot showing a sample KMS alias/ARN mapping (redacted).
- Platform-managed keys: default rotation cadence is 90 days for root platform keys; tenant-level wrappers are rotated on a 180-day cadence by default. Customers can request a custom cadence through a dedicated support/contracting flow; custom SLAs for rotation cadence are part of Dedicated/Private deployment discussions.

Action items for the call (we'll bring these artifacts):
- Walk the redwood-kms-ownership-diagram.pdf (boundary + tenant flow)
- Share a redacted rotation-audit-sample.log and an explanation of audit fields
- Provide a runbook excerpt showing responsibility matrix (platform vs BYOK)

If the proposed wording below works for you, confirm and we'll include it inline in your SIG answer: 
"Redwood does not retain customer private key material when customers opt for BYOK; references/ARNs to customer KMS are stored and used per integration agreements. For Redwood-managed keys, default rotation cadence is 90 days (platform) with tenant wrapper rotations at 180 days; customers can request custom cadences through account teams for Dedicated or Private deployments. All rotation events are logged to a tamper-evident audit trail which is available to customers under contractual terms"

I'll attach the diagram and checklist now to the thread.

—Irene

[Attachment: redwood-kms-ownership-diagram.pdf]
[Attachment: sig-evidence-checklist.xlsx]
